questions.correct: Picking a power and hoping, with no feedback
wrong: Measuring the real speed and correcting for it
Reading the encoder on every single loop
Spinning the wheel with two motors at once
questions.explain: Open-loop means you set a fixed power and hope it's right — no feedback. The motor doesn't know a shot just slowed it, so it can't react.

questions.q: The controller works like a car's...
wrong: Turn signal
Windshield wiper
Parking brake
questions.explain: Cruise control guesses the base throttle for the set speed, then corrects using the real speed. Feedforward + feedback is exactly that idea.

questions.correct: A smart starting guess for the power
wrong: A correction based on the current error
The encoder's raw tick-per-second count
The stick's deadzone threshold value
questions.explain: Feedforward (kV) is the physics-based guess: about 1/6000 power per RPM for this motor. kV * target lands the wheel near its speed with no measuring.

questions.correct: A correction based on how far off you are
wrong: A fixed guess made before spinning up
The number of encoder ticks per revolution
The target RPM the driver dials in
questions.explain: kP is feedback: the farther the real RPM is from target, the harder it pushes. It cleans up whatever the feedforward guess missed, like after a shot.

wrong: power = kV * error + kP * target
power = kV - kP + target
power = target / kV * kP
questions.explain: power = kV * targetRpm + kP * error, where error = targetRpm - actualRpm. The guess (kV*target) plus the correction (kP*error) holds the speed.

questions.correct: Target RPM minus the actual RPM
wrong: Actual RPM minus the target RPM
Target RPM times the actual RPM
The battery voltage minus the RPM
questions.explain: error = targetRpm - actualRpm — how far below (or above) target you are right now. A positive error means "too slow, add power."

questions.q: Why can kP be small when kV is good?
questions.correct: Feedforward already provides the baseline power
wrong: A small kP makes the motor spin faster
The rules limit how large kP is allowed
The battery can't handle a large kP
questions.explain: With feedforward supplying the baseline, kP only has to fix small disturbances — so it stays gentle. Without feedforward, kP does all the work and wobbles.

questions.q: What is the right tuning order?
questions.correct: Calibrate kV first with kP at zero, then raise kP
wrong: Raise kP first, then set kV back to zero
Set both of them to the maximum at once
Leave both at zero and just start firing
questions.explain: First set kP=0 and adjust kV until the RPM holds the target. Then raise kP until shots snap back without bouncing. kV first, kP second.

questions.q: What does too much kP cause?
questions.correct: Oscillation — bouncing above and below target
wrong: The wheel to spin up a lot slower
The battery to drain about twice as fast
The encoder to stop counting its ticks
questions.explain: Push kP too high and it overcorrects, so the RPM bounces above and below the target line. The sweet spot is a fast snap-back with no bounce.

questions.q: Why do flywheels usually skip the I term?
questions.correct: Feedforward removes lingering error, and I winds up
wrong: The I term makes the wheel spin backward
The I term is against the FTC competition rules
The battery cannot supply power to the I term
questions.explain: With good feedforward there's no lingering error for I to erase, and I tends to "wind up" and overshoot. So flywheels leave it out.

questions.q: Why do flywheels often skip or shrink the D term?
questions.correct: The speed reading is noisy and D amplifies noise
wrong: The D term slows the wheel down far too much
The D term drains the battery very quickly
The rules flatly forbid using the D term
questions.explain: The encoder's speed reading is a little noisy, and D reacts to how fast the error changes — so it amplifies that noise. Many teams skip it or keep it tiny.

questions.q: After the upgrade, the driver's trim now adjusts...
questions.correct: The target RPM, not the raw power
wrong: The raw power, not the target RPM
The encoder's ticks per revolution
The robot's heading read from the IMU
questions.explain: The controller sets power itself, so trimming power would get overwritten. Instead the trim nudges the target, and the controller holds whatever target you dial.

questions.q: What does kV roughly equal for this motor?
wrong: About 6000 divided by 1
Exactly 28 times 60
About 1 divided by 28
questions.explain: The motor hits about 6000 RPM at full power, so holding a speed needs about power = RPM/6000 — which makes kV ≈ 1/6000 (about 0.000167).

questions.q: What does the P stand for in PID?
wrong: Power
Position
Percent
questions.explain: PID is Proportional, Integral, Derivative. You built the Proportional part (plus feedforward), which is the sweet spot most flywheels use.

questions.q: Without feedforward, the kP term must...
questions.correct: Do all the work, so it gets jittery
wrong: Stay at exactly zero the whole time
Spin a second backup flywheel motor
Reset the encoder count every loop
questions.explain: With no feedforward baseline, kP has to supply all the power AND correct — so it needs to be large, which makes it overshoot and jitter. Feedforward keeps kP gentle.
